Baseline/gate reconciliation discipline from those cards applies if this repo grows the same checker (#5043 carries the prototype). (Triage seat, session `session_019gCKd9EZfQ6MbGTnMHHJvW`.)

Container & model: `L`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — 15 symbols × three possible dispositions across five documents and five packages, each decided against a **built** `dist/index.d.ts`. The volume is not the hard part; the per-name judgement is.
Clause-②: no — documentation and a ledger's reason text. No code, no exports, no contract.
Serial constraints cleared: nothing open touches any of the five documents or `scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs`. Note **PR5251 merged this round** and touched `content/docs/blocks/forms.mdx` — a different file; rebase and re-verify.

## Premise — the gate has LANDED since this card was written

The card was measured on the unlanded branch `claude/issue-5138-doc-snippet-compile-gate`. That gate is now **on `main`**: `scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` plus its test. So reproduce against `main`, not against a branch, and **re-measure the 15 diagnostics** — the card is ~13 hours old and a dozen PRs have landed since.

Take the name set from each package's **built `dist/index.d.ts`**, never from a grep of `src/`. The card gives the reason and it is a measured one: #5053 found `ReportScheduleConfig` appears twice in `src/` and is *not* exported, so a grep-based check calls a missing symbol real.

## ⛔ The scoping call the card does not make — read before planning

The card says *"Fixing a document is what lets its entry be deleted — the ledger can only shrink."* **That is not true for four of these five documents**, and I checked the ledger to be sure. Each entry lists far more than its TS2305s:

| document | ledger entry says |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/app-shell/README.md` | 1 parse + 18 undefined-name + **TS2305x2** |
| `packages/components/README.md` | 2 undefined-name + **TS2305x3** |
| `packages/core/README.md` | 5 undefined-name + **TS2305x6** + TS2351x1 |
| `content/docs/guide/objectos-integration.mdx` | 36 parse + 10 undefined-name + 7 unresolved-module + **TS2305x3** + TS2339x1 |

So fixing the TS2305s leaves every one of these still failing on other diagnostics, still ungated, and **its entry still required**. My ruling, so you are not left guessing:

1. **Fix the 15 TS2305s.** That is the card and it is worth doing on its own: four of these files ship to npm inside their package's `files`, so a reader who copies the import gets a compile error.
2. **Re-measure each touched document and UPDATE its `UNGATED_DOCS` reason text** to the new diagnostic mix. Leaving `TS2305x6` in `core`'s entry when there are zero is exactly the stale-ledger rot that has cost this seat repeatedly today. The entry text is the ledger's honesty.
3. **Delete an entry only if that document reaches zero diagnostics** — then the gate covers it and the ratchet has actually moved. Do not force this; do not "fix" unrelated parse diagnostics to chase a deletion.
4. ⛔ **Never add an entry, never widen one, never relax the gate.** Weakening a gate is maintainer-floor.

If none of the five reaches zero, that is a fine outcome — say so plainly. The deliverable is *the published pages stop teaching imports that do not exist*, not a shrunken ledger.

## The three dispositions — per name, not per batch

From #5053, and they are not interchangeable:

- **renamed** → re-spell it;
- **lives in a neighbour package** → fix the import path. The card flags the likely cluster: `PageSchema` / `FormSchema` / `InputSchema` / `BaseSchema` in `packages/core/README.md` are `@object-ui/types` vocabulary that `core` only *imports*;
- **removed with nothing replacing it** → delete the example and teach the real surface (the subtraction form of #5002 / PR5021).

**Report the disposition you chose for each of the 15 names, with the evidence.** A table is fine. That record is what makes the next document in this family cheap, and it is how a reviewer checks you did not simply delete the awkward ones.

## Size — partial delivery is explicitly allowed here

This is larger than a normal card. If the re-measure turns up materially more than 15, or a name's disposition needs a ruling you cannot make from the export surface alone (e.g. a symbol that should arguably be exported rather than the doc changed — **that is a contract question, not yours**), then:

- deliver the names you *can* settle,
- open the PR with **`Part of #5160`**, ⛔ **not** `Fixes #5160`, so merging does not silently close the card,
- and report exactly which names are left and why.

A truthful partial beats a rushed whole. ⛔ Do not "fix" a missing export by adding the export.

## Verification

- Re-run the gate over the changed documents and show before/after diagnostics per file.
- The gate's own test must stay green — remember `scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` has a test at `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-snippet-types.test.ts`. **Running the script is not running its test**; that exact gap turned PR5244 red today. Run both.
- Building is required: the gate compiles against built `dist`, so use `pnpm exec turbo run build $(node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs --build-filter)`.

## Gates

Derive from your diff. `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is **objectstack-only**. Expect `Doc Snippet Type Check`, `Internal Docs Link Check`, `Build Docs`, `Control Byte Scan`. Changeset: run `check-changeset-presence.mjs` and follow its verdict — READMEs sit inside published packages, so do not assume either way.

⛔ **Do not background a long check and end your turn.** Narrow and declare the narrowing if the shared verify lock is contended.

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first body line `Fixes #5160` **or** `Part of #5160` per the size note above. Push the branch early. Return the JSON report and post it as a comment whose first line is the literal `<!-- os-dev-report -->` marker.

**14 of 15 delivered in PR5260 (`Part of`, not `Fixes`). The 15th — `AppManifest` — needs a ruling.** PM round 6, session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`. This card **stays open**; it flips to `needs-user-decision` when PR5260 merges.

## Why the last one is not the same kind of problem as the other fourteen

The other fourteen were name problems: renamed, in a neighbour package, or fabricated. `AppManifest` is **a wrong-shape problem**, and that makes the cheap fix actively harmful.

The name exists — at `@objectstack/spec/system`, not the root subpath the guide imports from. But `AppManifestSchema` is:

```
name, label, version, description?, objects: string[]  // object NAMES
views: string[], flows: string[], dependencies: string[]
```

and the literal it annotates has **no `label`**, and its `objects` is a **map of full object definitions** (`{ contact: { name, label, fields: {…} } }`), plus `pages` and `navigation`. That is stack-config vocabulary wearing an app-manifest annotation.

**So fixing the import path alone trades TS2305 for a fresh TS2739/TS2322 on the same lines** — the page still teaches something that does not compile, while the ledger reads as improved. That is the one option I would rule out on my own authority.

## The options

- **A. Rewrite to `defineStack`** — the repo's own canonical form for this exact filename, documented in `packages/types/src/index.ts`. Verified by the dev: `ObjectStackDefinitionInput` accepts the map format the literal already uses (the raw schema rejects maps; `defineStack` normalises them). **Cost**: `name`/`version`/`description` move into `manifest`, `pages[].component` needs re-expressing, and **`navigation` has no top-level home** — it must be dropped or relocated under a plugin's `navigationContributions`.
- **B. Fix only the path.** Ruled out above.
- **C. Delete the block and link to the framework repo's documentation.** This repo's own docs already say the file lives there — `content/docs/guide/console.md:72` and `console-architecture.md:75` both state it explicitly.
- **D. Leave it.** What PR5260 does pending your answer; the ledger entry keeps `TS2305x1`.

## The argument I find strongest, which is the dev's

**C, then A if the framework repo has no such page.** The decisive fact is that this block documents a **server-project config file this repo does not own and cannot build** — four of its runtime imports (`@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-app`, `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`) are unresolvable here and account for 7 of the page's TS2307s. **Nobody can follow this page end-to-end from objectui alone**, so a faithful rewrite would serve a scenario that does not exist at this address.

And the durability point: **this page is ungated and will stay ungated** (36 parse diagnostics). A rewritten block would drift silently and be wrong again in a month. C removes the drift surface; A fossilises a copy of another repo's contract in a repo that cannot check it.

## Worth noting about the rest of the delivery

The ledger discipline I set held, and produced one honest surprise: `packages/core/README.md`'s diagnostic mix went **up** in one category. Not a regression — with `defineView` unresolved, `userListView` was an error type and two `.push` lines were never type-checked at all. Fixing the import is what surfaced them. Filed as **#5257** rather than absorbed.

Three findings filed rather than folded in: **#5257** (`cloneAsOverride` keeps its input's deep-readonly type, so the documented override clone does not type-check), **#5258** (`new ComponentRegistry()` — it is a singleton instance, not a class), **#5259** (`packages/components/README.md` is one declared fragment from leaving the ledger, but covering it pulls four packages into the gate's build filter — a cost decision under the #4846 ruling, correctly not taken as a rider).
